findings.summary: 2-XL is an educational robot toy marketed 1978–1981 by Mego Corporation and 1992–1995 by Tiger Electronics. It was the first "smart-toy" with rudimentary intelligence, memory, and gameplay. The toy used 8-track cartridges (Mego) or cassette tapes (Tiger) containing multiple-choice questions answered via buttons. Its "personality" was generated by a synthesizer creating a high-pitched robot voice, augmented by jokes and verbal reinforcements. The name is a pun on "to excel." The toy responded verbally to button choices, offering encouragement or teasing depending on correctness.

mechanisms.title: Decision-tree tape navigation
mechanisms.explanation: Buttons (YES/NO or A/B/C) changed the tape tracking on 8-track cartridges or selected tracks on cassette tapes, allowing the toy to branch to different responses based on user input.

mechanisms.title: Synthesizer-driven personality
mechanisms.explanation: A synthesizer modulated the inventor's voice into a high-pitched robot sound; pre-recorded lines provided praise, teasing, or second chances, creating the impression of interactive responsiveness.

unknowns: Exact internal logic governing tape-tracking decisions
How multiple-choice options were mapped to specific tape segments
Details of the personality algorithm beyond recorded lines
Mechanism for battery operation in the Tiger Electronics version
